text:
maya: Quick heads-up — we're planning to change the public metering aggregation window from per-minute to hourly rollups for billing and invoice line items. Target cutover: 2026-05-12 PST. This should reduce invoice noise for bursty workloads and simplify downstream accounting. It WILL affect how free trial credits are consumed, so we need coordinated comms.

zane: Clarifying Q — does this change runtime rate limiting or burst enforcement (per-route)?

maya: Good Q. No, rate limiting and realtime throttles remain per-minute for enforcement and SLOs. This change only affects metering/aggregation used for billing, invoice lines, and CSV exports. :white_check_mark:

finance-bot: RFC + migration plan: https://redwood.internal/rfc/hourly-metering-v2 — TL;DR: (1) invoice aggregation window = 1 hour; (2) free trial credits recalibrated to preserve expected lifetime; (3) proration rules updated for mid-cycle plan changes. Simulation run planned.

alex: For Dedicated / committed customers — will committed capacity reporting or invoices show any unexpected variance? We need to avoid surprises for partners.

maya: For Dedicated customers we will keep per-minute observability in the Console (metrics & live usage). Invoices will show consolidated hourly lines but include a per-route breakdown CSV export for auditing. We'll run a 30-day side-by-side validation comparing minute vs hour billing to flag divergences.

ops: High level rollout dates + impact on monitoring/alerts?

maya: Rollout plan in RFC (summary):
- 2026-04-20: migrate analytics pipeline to support hourly aggregation (dry-run).
- 2026-04-27 -> 2026-05-10: side-by-side billing simulation (no invoice changes, dispatch validation reports).
- 2026-05-12: switch invoice aggregation to hourly (switch flips; invoices generated after this date will use hourly lines).
- 2026-06-15: finalize audits and deprecate legacy minute line-items for billing exports.

zane: Will free tier behavior change? e.g., the 30k free tokens/month — could hourly aggregation make trial credits burn faster?

maya: We expect that naive hourly rollups could accelerate trial consumption for high-frequency small requests. To avoid that, we're implementing "credit-smoothing" to approximate previous per-request credit consumption over an hour window. Example pseudocode in the RFC: 
```
# credit smoothing pseudocode
for each customer, for each hour:
  raw_tokens = sum(tokens_per_request)
  smoothed = max(raw_tokens, ceil(raw_tokens * smoothing_factor))
  allocate_credits(smoothed)
```
This preserves trial lifetime for most patterns.

finance-bot: Billing export change: new column "metering_window" will be added with values: "minute" or "hour". Early adopters can request minute-mode exports via support for a 90-day window post-cutover.

alex: Need written comms for partners + a support playbook; also check contract clauses for committed usage.

maya: Agreed. Draft customer email and support playbook are live: https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/hourly-rollout-playbook — @billing-team please review and sign off by 2026-04-15.

billing-team: On it. We'll review committed-customer contract language and propose amendment suggestions if needed.

ops: Concern — will pipeline ingest/backfill cause higher dashboard latency? The change sounds heavy.

maya: The pipeline change is additive and uses hourly batching to reduce long-term ingest. Staging dashboards will be available next week for ops validation. Backfills (simulation) will run on a separate queue to avoid production dashboard impact.

zane: Small request — can we expose a rollback toggle in the Console for the first 14 days post-cutover? Might help incident rollforward.

maya: Noted. We'll add a runtime toggle with audit logging and a 14-day safeguard window.

maya: Next steps for this thread: billing + ops to review RFC, engineering to run 7-day simulation, comms to finalize emails. I'll post a short status update after the dry-run on 2026-04-21. Thanks everyone. :pray:
